Params: Every seat beneath the dome is occupied, and the noise of the crowd is deafening. Shifting prismatic images glide across the center of the arena, their mirrored surfaces catching the faces of the eager audience in endless repetition.
The holographic host appears at the heart of the space, poised to begin.
Esteemed faculty, cadets, ladies and gentlemen, the World Military Academy Joint Combat Competition is about to begin here today at the F.O.S. arena!
This year's champion will receive direct admission to the World Government's military ranks, with no assessments or sponsorship required.
Thunderous applause fills the arena as the contestants enter the floor in single file, the F.O.S. anthem playing overhead.
In the stands, a white-haired girl sits still and silent, her composure untouched. The excitement of the crowd flows around her like water around a stubborn stone.
She leans forward, scanning the line of the contestants.
A streak of blue passes through the ranks.
Her face, once soft with youth, now carries something sharp and determined in the arena's light. In her eyes, a golden trophy glimmers.
I'm going to win this, and I'm going to make it look easy. That trophy's mine.
Thirty-two teams. Almost a hundred people... Arakna, this is F.O.S. The best there is. Beating them means beating—
The whole world, right? Which is exactly why I'm here at ten at night, training like a maniac.
I don't have a choice. This door opens for anyone. And going straight into the military is the only way I reach a platform where I can actually change something.
Adelyde asked a question that both of them already knew the answer to. F.O.S. had a stellar engineering track, and yet Arakna had chosen tactics. That alone said everything.
Running from everything doesn't make you free. I know that now.
Arakna looked away, as though she could still see the stars she had dreamed of as a child, lingering just beyond her reach.
For a moment, neither of them spoke. The only sound was the continuous crack of gunfire from the training grounds.
After graduation, I'm going back to my family. The military isn't my path.
Of course. Maybe we were never meant to walk the same road, not from the very start.
A cold smile appeared on Arakna's face, but the words that followed were marked by bitterness.
Adelyde did not respond to the remark. She reached into a paper bag and pulled out a small bottle made by hand.
It was cast in clear resin, and inside it sat a crooked little starship, roughly made, with two wings of uneven size.
Interstellar Drift Bottle. You told me about it.
Arakna's rigid smile dissolved into a burst of laughter, broad and unreserved, almost childish in its abandon.
Adelyde recognized it. It belonged to the girl who had once flown beside her on the Kelpie, laughing into the wind.
But that time had long passed.
The laughter faded, and Arakna straightened, her composure restored as quickly as it had slipped.
I don't want anything from a Helio.
She angled her body like she was about to walk away, yet she stayed in place, as though she expected something more.
Arakna reached out and snatched the small, ugly bottle from her.
Ana! Training's started! How long has this break been?
After the competition, I'll teach you how to make a good one.
Adelyde returns from the memory that's months old now. Her hand tightens around her own wrist, and her expression clouds with a complexity she cannot untangle.
Next, let's welcome this year's official representatives.

The World Government General Staff. The Science Council Joint Military Exercise Simulation Technicians. The Kowloong Corp Pulao Crew. The Arctic Route Union Military Commission. The Akdilek Commercial Alliance Upper Carriage Delegates. And—
Suited figures take their seats in the VIP section one after another. A tall woman in a white Helio uniform moves among them, each step sharp and deliberate.
A flash of joy follows, the kind a child feels when they catch a parent's face in the crowd at a school gathering.
But the warmth fades quickly, replaced by a quieter unease. When Rusalka appears in public as the Helios' blade, it is seldom a sign of good news.
The arena takes a break after two matches. Adelyde stands and makes her way toward the VIP passage.
She stops short at the turn.
In the dim passage, Rusalka is talking to someone she recognizes, a face that has passed through her memory just once or twice.
Arakna's friend and partner in this competition, Alyssa.
The girl keeps her head down, clutching a folded paper. Rusalka says something, and Alyssa nods and moves away.
Adelyde takes the other corner, waits, and when Rusalka emerges toward the VIP seats, she steps forward.
She is still three steps away when Rusalka pivots and looks directly at her, catching the surprise on Adelyde's face.
How did you know it was me, Miss Rusalka?
Your footsteps. I know the child I've trained.
Heh... No. You're a grown woman now, ready to do real work with me.
I thought you might be competing. Would've been a chance to see if you've improved or fallen behind.
But... since you've chosen not to pursue the military, that means you've decided, haven't you?
You're about to graduate. With your F.O.S. credentials and our family's ties to the Transatlantic Economic Community's military districts, you're better positioned than anyone else in the family.
You'll need to learn to oversee the energy lines, from the Atlantic Eye to the South Atlantic branches. Quarterly production reports, personnel transfers. I'll walk you through it all.
The head of the family will announce retirement soon. A seat on the Council will open for Helios. We can't afford to miss it.
There's a seat for you beside me in the TEC stands. Sitting there would send the right message.
Adelyde meets those jade eyes, unchanged from years past. Stern and unyielding as always, with something deeper beneath them that she still cannot read.
Our next match is about to begin! Contestants, to your positions!
Representing the red side, Team 09: two special admissions from the South Atlantic, and one technical genius from the Transatlantic Economic Community.
Arakna Sorano, number one globally in the special admissions exam. Alyssa Lin, number ten worldwide. Aristo Colman, tactical coordinator, engineering prodigy, with full-field drone vision.
All three have posted S-rank evaluations in multiple simulations over the past year. Without question, this team is the favorite to win it all tonight—

Voices rise for Arakna's devastating barrage, for Alyssa's clever strategy, and from one corner, a huddle of technical students debates the performance of Aristo's drone swarm... Adelyde absorbs the whole scene.
Adelyde has her fingers crossed and lets the words run quietly through her mind.
Below, Alyssa steps into the center of the arena and takes the microphone.
Sorry, everyone. Due to personal reasons—
I'm pulling out of this competition.
She looks over at Arakna. The girl's image is already projected on the main display, her expression mirroring Adelyde's disbelief.
Before the entire crowd, Alyssa steps around Arakna's reaching hand and heads directly for the contestant tunnel.
An unforeseen turn of events! With the withdrawal of Alyssa Lin, Team 09's Assault, the team is down to only two members, one short of the required three.
Per competition rules, any team reduced below three members by personal withdrawal will face immediate elimination!
Elimination. Everything Arakna had endured, every drop of effort she had poured into these years, wiped out by a single decision?
Arakna's speech. Alyssa's abrupt withdrawal. Rusalka's quiet meeting with Alyssa. The images pass through Adelyde's mind in rapid succession.

Around her, the stands are buzzing with confusion, but she hears none of it. The arena's red and gold fade from her focus. Her body turns to stone, and she is back in that grim docking port from years past.
And I'd watch the people around her. She's got guts, and others may not. The ones cheering today could be the ones selling her out tomorrow.
She refuses to believe that the fortress she had chosen, the one meant to shield humanity's future, would allow the hands of vested interest to reach inside.

She refuses even more to believe that the home and the teacher who once shaped her understanding of will and honor would stoop to any measure to stamp out dissent in this arena, the very ground where those principles were meant to be upheld.
Yet internal erosion always outpaces external siege, and she has never been unaware of what it means to stand against the family she belongs to.
In the middle of the arena, the blue-haired girl catches the retreating figure by the arm.
Please, I need to know. This is important!
The girl whose wrist is held removes her earpiece with measured calm and speaks, her words meant only for the other.

Do you even know that one of the TEC sponsorships you got shut down with your investigation was mine? I haven't even asked you why you took what belonged to me. And you're standing here asking me why?
Arakna, I'm my family's hope too. We're just each looking out for ourselves.
I couldn't say no to the last chance that woman gave me.
Alyssa turns her face aside and speaks quickly, as though she fears any pause might invite an objection.
Arakna falters, caught off guard, and her hold loosens. Alyssa slips away without a second's delay.
The glare from the arena floods her vision, and a sharp surge of dizziness passes through her. Her head dips under its weight.
Someone offered Alyssa everything Arakna was accused of taking from her. The price was simple: withdraw from the match, in front of everyone.
All of it, to break her future, to make their authority plain to the world. They would do anything to prove their hold.
She delivers her final words in a trembling voice, then turns and hurries toward the exit as if running from something. Arakna is left standing there, alone.
A substitution window is now open. Any currently enrolled student who has not yet registered may step forward to fill the vacancy.
That said, any substitute must be vouched for in person by an instructor.
If those requirements cannot be met, the team will forfeit its eligibility.
The blue-haired girl stands at the center of the arena, her head bowed, her shadow pinned small and insignificant under the glare.
Then she lifts her gaze. Her eyes sweep the stands, row after row, until they stop on the family section. In them, a fury burns bright enough to ignite the air.
Just now, right here, in the arena of one of the best academies humanity has ever built, someone used a sponsorship to threaten my teammate.
They didn't even want us to lose. They wanted to make sure we never got the chance!
They picked today. They picked here. In front of the entire world... It's a message to all of you: talk too much truth, push back too hard, and this is what happens to you.
Her voice carries through the speakers, echoing beneath the dome. In the family section, row after row of suited figures sit without moving a single inch.
The three of us trained a whole year for this. Over three hundred days and nights, we gave everything, just to prove—
Her voice is cut short without warning. In the shadows of the family section, someone has just lowered a terminal.
And they have done it again, in plain sight of everyone.
The crowd breaks into an uproar.
We gave everything, just to prove—
The next second, she rips the useless earpiece from her ear, flings it to the ground, and screams into the stands with everything she has left.
—Everyone has the right to define their own future!
So I'm asking. Is there anyone who'll walk this path with me?!
She calls out with clarity, but the microphone is gone. Her voice, though strong, cuts through the air briefly before being swallowed by the crowd's clamor.
Right then, a trembling figure moves into the open floor.
It's Aristo, the one who always fears getting hurt, the one who always shrinks from the crowd. Now he stands beside Arakna, his face pale as paper, but he does not step away.
Even someone like me hasn't backed down! Standing here... isn't so scary!
We just need one more. P-please, someone, stand with us!
She rises from the family section like a polished blade drawn from its sheath.
Rusalka's hand locks around her wrist at once, the grip hard enough to leave marks.
Adelyde looks into those jade eyes and sees a warning that allows no dispute.
She feels herself pinned under the gaze of a giant. If that thing had a name, she would call it the Family Machine.
Those who hold its reins can decide life or death for whomever they wish.
The giant has just crushed a life under its heel without care, and a bone-chilling cry rises from beneath its foot.
Now those enormous, unfathomable, terrifying eyes turn to her. They hold no anger or hatred. Only an offer.
Join it, or be cast beyond its reach forever.
Her hand closes around Rusalka's with equal force, answering firmness with firmness.
She walks down from the family seats, step by heavy step.
The stairs feel like they will never end.
Against the dark sky, the Kelpie cut through the waves, its bow light swaying in the storm.
At Port A054, a dark crowd pushed past her. She walked against the current in her white uniform, and no one met her eyes.
The port was empty. Morning light fell across the dam, across her alone.
So she keeps walking forward, alone.
Through two years of training grounds,
intelligence threads, and the prep area where she loads her magazines alone.
She reaches the center of the arena, takes Arakna's hand, and lifts it into the air.
Have you lost your mind? What are you doing?!
Mt mind is perfectly clear. I believe everything you said. Everyone has the right to define their own future.
"The distance between us is real. But that's not going to stop me from reaching out." Someone told me that once.
She extends her hand to Arakna.
The blue-haired girl clenches her jaw and takes it firmly.
The tide turns again! Team 09 has found their substitute, Adelyde Helio, third-year Tactics.
Now, will any instructor vouch for her participation?
Across the arena, a young instructor in black-rimmed glasses rises from the faculty seats, his voice loud and clear.

Wells Adelman, vouching with my full authority as instructor. I affirm that Adelyde Helio's decision is fair, rational, and sound. I'll sign any documents requiring an instructor's signature for her entry.
It starts in a single corner and spreads outward. One person, then two... then ten, then a hundred. Students rise from their seats, clapping in unison.
The ovation rolls through the arena like thunder.

In the family section, the figures in white stand as one and exit in silence. If any lens were trained on them at this moment, it would catch a collection of faces drawn tight with displeasure, almost laughable in their rigidity.
I therefore officially announce that Team 09 is reinstated for the competition.
The next match begins now. Prepare yourselves!
Later That Night, Outside the Arena
Adelyde says goodbye to her companions, glances at the shadows under the lights, and steps in alone.
A crushing force comes at her, enough to freeze even the most seasoned fighter.
She does not flinch. Her neck is caught, and she is thrown back against the cold wall.
I still have a match tomorrow.
Do you have any idea what you've done?!

You walked out of the family stands in front of every faction representative and stood beside that student. You've openly challenged the entire Transatlantic Economic Community. The Great Family Council can lock you out permanently, any time they want.
And that's the best-case scenario. For what?
"Friendship"? "Justice"? You're no different from some dock kid throwing punches over a piece of candy.
The words are shaped like a question, but Adelyde's voice carries no uncertainty.
...Come back with me now. We can still fix this; say it was a moment of youthful recklessness. Adelyde, this is your last chance.
Adelyde offers no defense. Her eyes meet Rusalka's without heat, without flinching. Rusalka has braced for rage or fear, but she finds neither.
Instead, there is only distance, as though the girl stands on a far shore, looking back at a figure she no longer knows.
The quiet in that gaze is what breaks the last of Rusalka's composure. The blade comes out, cold and quick, stopping a hair's breadth from her throat.
Adelyde holds still. She does not blink.
The weapon stays at the brink, held by a hand that refuses to follow through.
Power can freeze a person's status, take away their life's work, even their life.
But it can't touch what someone believes in.
This isn't the Transatlantic Economic Community. This is F.O.S.
Do you really believe that walking through that door makes you one of them?
Adelyde, your soul was forged by the Transatlantic Economic Community. We are your own kind.
...I have the right and the power to define who I am.
The blade lowers, and the steel clicks back into its sheath.
Rusalka speaks, her tone as cold as the lightless deep.
Then as of today, you will be marked internally as a traitor to the family.
Your family name stays. Everything else, including every title, every access privilege, every position as heir, will be gone.
After graduation, you'll still serve the family, but at the edges, surrounded by failures and scraps. You will never be allowed to enter the Atlantic Eye again. Not even approach it.
One last time. This is just me now, your teacher. I want my student to come back to the right path.
Say yes, and come with me.
She closes her eyes, a shudder passing through her as she exhales. She takes a step back and bends in a deep, formal bow toward Rusalka.
...Thank you for all your years of guidance, Miss Rusalka.

You taught me how to wield strength, how to stand straight when there's no way forward. Never break in an endgame, never bend when trapped, never surrender in a deadlock. Those lessons are in my blood. They're what shaped me.
Even if you and the Helio family cut me off completely, I will carry those lessons with me forever.
The white-haired figure turns away from the shadows and heads toward the F.O.S. square. There, countless lamps are still lit against the night, their glow catching in her crystalline eyes.
<size=60>She has nothing to look back to.</size>
